## Grounding — future #66 fallback (read-only)

**Base:** `/home/iseoane/Work/isSWF` at `d352b58`; working tree was clean. This is source grounding only, not implementation.

### What is represented now

`docs/model-routing.md` names [`.factory/models.json`](.factory/models.json) as canonical. Routes are ordered arrays of `{model, effort}` tuples; there is no separate “primary” field, retry counter, or permission field. At this checkpoint, `worker` and `reviewer` each have only Luna/high; `researcher` has GLM 5.3 Flash/high followed by Luna/medium; `additional-review` has DeepSeek/max. Thus the researcher route is the only configured alternate, but its presence alone authorizes neither execution nor cost. Routes are pinned per attempt; changes affect future attempts only. (`.factory/models.json`; `docs/model-routing.md:5–17`)

The current guide permits advancing only to the **next configured tuple**, after confirmed unavailability or exhausted quota/capacity, and only if the trusted grant permits it. It requires preflight of the selected tuple’s support, effort compatibility, and availability; it prohibits skipping ahead. (`docs/model-routing.md:5,13–17`)

### Budget and operator decisions

The spec approves the **policy shape**: bounded retries for temporary transport/availability failures, no retry on quota exhaustion, and a total attempt limit that does not reset on provider change. But its proposed defaults—one temporary retry per destination and two correction rounds—are explicitly “defaults nuevos para revisar,” not settled values. No numeric total-attempt budget is represented in the route schema or current guide. (`docs/spec-v1.md:198–227`)

Already specified: no fallback for test failures, review findings, poor output, or incorrect implementation; no silent effort downgrade, extra provider, or added cost. Unavailable credentials, incompatibility, or denied permission block. (`docs/spec-v1.md:198–205`; `docs/model-routing.md:15`)

**Still requires an actual operator decision before implementation can treat it as policy:** numeric total-attempt/retry budget; which role routes and fallback tuple(s) are approved for the job; and any cost/provider authorization not already explicit in the trusted grant. Configuration membership is not permission. The fallback concept in #66 is approved, but these concrete values and grants are not established by these sources.

### Minimal future caller contract and #68 prerequisite

A fallback caller needs the pinned config path + full input SHA, role and complete resolved ordered route, selected tuple, requested/observed model and effort, evidence for availability/failure classification, transition reason, and remaining total-attempt budget. Before starting the next tuple it must establish the previous writer **stopped**, reconcile identity/task/ownership and partial work, and confirm the next tuple and actor remain authorized. Coordinator rules expressly prohibit replacement on `unknown` state or identity. (`docs/model-routing.md:7,15–17`; coordinator skill §5, especially lines 59, 66, 75)

Keep failure classes distinct: **confirmed provider unavailability/quota** may advance; **credentials, compatibility, or permission failure** blocks; **unknown process state or uncertain remote effect** blocks until reconciled. A timeout, tool error, or model prose alone does not prove quota exhaustion or absence of effects. #68 must first supply reliable cessation evidence and partial-effect reconciliation; fallback must not invent recovery semantics.

### Acceptance

Verify ordered-route pinning and tuple efforts; authorized confirmed-quota/unavailable transition with recorded reason; no transition on tests/review/quality failures; incompatibility, denied permission, unknown state, active writer, or unresolved effects block; exhausted route/budget blocks; configuration changes do not rewrite active attempts. These align with S03 and `MOD-01`–`MOD-06`. (`docs/plan-v1.md:53, S03`; `docs/spec-v1.md:229–234`)
limitations: report says clean working tree but known untracked artifacts existed; no cleanliness claim adopted
